title: Odisha cooks with fire
lead: A blistered vegetable, an opened leaf parcel, a browned edge. Follow the heat into three food stories—and leave room for the cook’s own version.
intro: Fire leaves different signatures. Start with roasted vegetables, then open a leaf parcel. Continue to baked dishes and notice how the method changes the story. These are documented preparations to explore, with real photographs and named accounts.

chapters.title: Beneath the blistered skin
chapters.text: Follow eggplant from flame to mash, with a photograph that shows its tomato companion.

chapters.title: A small bowl at the edge
chapters.text: Find bilati poda beside pakhala, then ask which name and preparation the cook knows.

chapters.title: Open the parcel
chapters.text: Mushroom, fish or prawn? The ingredient, leaf and cooking method each deserve a question.

questions: How is the heat used: direct roasting, a wrapped parcel, or baking?
contribution: Tell us about a preparation you know: its name, ingredients, method, place and the person who makes it. Share photographs and memories with permission.
limits: A reading collection, not a fixed traditional meal, statewide origin claim or verified restaurant trail. Odia names and household variants await local review. The lead photograph combines eggplant and tomato.
eyebrow: Food, fire & the people behind a meal
onward_text: Continue to Poda pitha and Chhena poda. Their pages explain the preparations; a shared word does not make every cooking method the same.
